dv1_sovereignty_tests.topic: What sovereignty means: Montevideo and Krasner

claims.text: The Montevideo Convention, signed on 26 December 1933, says a state as a person of international law should possess a permanent population, a defined territory, government, and capacity to enter into relations with other states (Article 1).

Article 3 of the Convention says the political existence of a state is independent of recognition by other states; Article 8 says no state has the right to intervene in the internal or external affairs of another.

Stephen Krasner argued in Sovereignty: Organized Hypocrisy (1999) that states have never been as sovereign as supposed, that rulers mainly want to stay in power, and that differences in power and interests, not international norms, best explain state behaviour; he called the pattern of long-standing but frequently violated norms 'organized hypocrisy'.

Krasner distinguishes four meanings of sovereignty: domestic (exclusive legal authority within a territory), interdependence (capacity to control transnational flows), international legal (recognition of juridically autonomous territorial entities) and Westphalian (exclusion of external actors from domestic authority structures).

dv1_three_cities_status.topic: The three cities' legal status and size, compared

claims.text: Vatican City's area is given as 49 hectares (0.49 km²) in some references and 44 hectares (109 acres) in others; the difference traces to a 1930 atlas that listed 44 ha and was corrected to 49 ha in 1945–1946.
Vatican City had 882 residents in 2024, regardless of citizenship, and 372 Vatican citizens living elsewhere, mostly diplomats and cardinals in Rome.

Vatican City is an elective absolute monarchy in which the pope holds executive, legislative and judicial power; Pope Leo XIV was elected on 8 May 2025. The Lateran Treaty was signed on 11 February 1929 and took effect on 7 June 1929.

The Holy See, the authority the Pope holds over the Catholic Church, is distinct from Vatican City, the enclave in Rome over which the Holy See has direct sovereignty; the Holy See has full diplomatic relations with 184 states plus the European Union and the Order of Malta.

The Holy See has been a permanent observer state at the United Nations since 6 April 1964 and has chosen not to seek membership; it is a full member of several UN specialized agencies, including WIPO, the ITU and the UPU.

The City of London covers 1.12 square miles (2.90 km²) and had 8,583 residents at the 2021 census; it is surrounded by Greater London but remains separate from its boroughs, and as a ceremonial county its Commission of Lieutenancy is headed by the Lord Mayor rather than a Lord-Lieutenant.
The Inner Temple and Middle Temple, inside the City's boundaries, are two of the few remaining 'liberties', treated as independent, extra-parochial enclaves.
The US Census Bureau estimated the District of Columbia's population at 693,645 on 1 July 2025, on 61.13 square miles of land.

Article I, Section 8, Clause 17 of the US Constitution gives Congress power 'to exercise exclusive Legislation in all Cases whatsoever, over such District (not exceeding ten Miles square)' as becomes the seat of government by cession of particular states.
Over the District Congress holds the blended powers of a local and a national legislature; it is neither required to provide an elected local government nor barred from delegating its powers to one.

Local elections existed almost from the start: an elected mayor from 1820; elected government ended after financial scandals in 1874; a presidentially appointed Commission ruled from 1878 and an appointed Mayor-Commissioner and council from 1967, before Congress restored limited elected self-government.

District residents vote for President and Vice President under the Twenty-third Amendment and elect a nonvoting delegate to Congress; a constitutional amendment to give them voting representation in Congress failed ratification.

dv1_police_and_force.topic: Who polices each city, and who answers for it

claims.text: The District of Columbia Home Rule Act, P.L. 93-198, approved on 24 December 1973, provided for a popularly elected mayor and council that could legislate and manage the city's affairs.
Most District laws take effect only after a 30-day layover for congressional review, counting only days when Congress is in session; laws in the criminal titles of the D.C. Code lie over for 60 days.

All District spending must be approved through the federal appropriations process, and Congress has more often shaped District affairs through appropriations riders than through disapproval resolutions.

Congress has enacted resolutions disapproving District acts three times under the Home Rule Act: the Location of Chanceries Act (1979), the Sexual Assault Reform Act (1981) and the Schedule of Heights Amendment Act (1990).

The Vatican's Corps of Gendarmerie was founded in 1816 by Pope Pius VII; it had 122 sworn members in 2022 and handles security, public order, border control, traffic and criminal investigation under the Governorate of Vatican City State, and hosts Interpol's national bureau for Vatican City.

The Pontifical Swiss Guard dates its founding to 22 January 1506 under Pope Julius II; it was enlarged from 110 to 135 members in 2019. Recruits must be unmarried Catholic Swiss men aged 19 to 30, at least 174 cm tall, who have completed Swiss military basic training.

The Police Act 1996 lists the City of London police area as one of the police areas of England and Wales, provides that the Common Council 'is to continue to be the police authority' for it, requires the Common Council to issue a policing plan each year, and requires the Commissioner of Police for the City of London to report to the Common Council.

dv1_holy_see_public_record.topic: The Holy See's public record toward Zionism, as markers for the front test

claims.text: Pius X received Theodor Herzl in private audience on 25 January 1904 and told him he could not support Zionism, saying that because the Jews had not recognized Christ, 'we cannot recognize the Jewish people'; the account rests on Herzl's diaries.

In the encyclical Redemptoris Nostri Cruciatus of 15 April 1949, Pius XII asked that Jerusalem and its vicinity be 'accorded and legally guaranteed an "international" status' (para. 9), urged Catholics to press for a juridical status for the city (para. 10), and asked that the other holy places be protected by an international agreement (para. 12).
